program_name: Language Technologies and Digital Humanities (official English name used identically on the programme microsite, on en.unito.it and on Apply@UniTo; UNITO internal course code 2713M22)
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale; UNITO 'Key information' states 'Type of course: Second Cycle Degree (Postgraduate)', 'Nominal Duration: 2 years - 120 CFU'; Apply@UniTo lists 'Type: POSTGRADUATE DEGREE, full-time', '2 years ... (120 ECTS)'. Apply@UniTo adds that for each year of enrolment students may choose between full-time and part-time status, with tuition fees varying accordingly)
teaching_language: Case (1) - fully English-taught. It is a stand-alone UNITO second-cycle degree of the Department of Humanities (Dipartimento di Studi Umanistici) / School of Human Sciences, not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree and not an interuniversity or joint degree. UNITO 'Key information' records 'Teaching Language: English' for a.y. 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26 alike, and Apply@UniTo records 'Study language: English'. Note that the programme name itself is English on the Italian pages too. IMPORTANT NUANCE: 'Key information' also records 'Teaching mode: Blended', i.e. classes are delivered in a mixed in-person/online format, and the admission interview is likewise held 'in blended mode' / by telematic (Webex) connection - this concerns delivery mode, not language.
campus: Turin (Torino), Piedmont, Italy. UNITO 'Key information': 'Teaching seat: Torino/Turin, Piedmont, Italy'; Apply@UniTo: 'Study location: Italy, Turin', 'Department of Humanities'. Administering structures: Department of Humanities (Dipartimento di Studi Umanistici), School of Human Sciences, with the Humanities Libraries as supporting structure. Student services e-mail: servizistudenti.scienzeumanistiche@unito.it. Teaching mode is 'Blended'.
degree_class: LM-43 - Metodologie informatiche per le discipline umanistiche (Computing Methods for the Humanities / Digital Humanities). Stated as 'Degree Program Class: LM-43' on the UNITO 'Key information' page for a.y. 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26. UNITO course code: 2713M22. Cineca national course catalogue ids: 35176 (2025 edition), 17104 (2024 edition).
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS (non-restricted number of places) WITH A COMPULSORY ADMISSION INTERVIEW AND DOSSIER EVALUATION. The programme's own admission page states: 'The Master's Degree Course in Language Technologies and Digital Humanities has non-restricted access. Enrollment can only take place after passing an interview aimed at verifying the adequacy of personal preparation of the candidates.' Consistently, on Apply@UniTo the programme appears in the 'Fourth admission call for open access postgraduate degree programs only'. There is no TOLC, no SAT and no written entrance examination. Admission is decided by a Commission of at least three teachers of the degree course, on the basis of a presentation dossier plus an interview. A separate territorial quota exists for one category only: 'This Master's degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.'
application_deadline_eu: A.Y. 2026/2027 - two distinct routes. (a) Applicants holding a FOREIGN qualification who are EU citizens/equivalents or non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy apply through Apply@UniTo. Usable calls: First admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 (open to all applicants for postgraduate degree programmes) and Fourth admission call for open-access postgraduate degree programmes only, 25 August - 8 September 2026, expressly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy'. The live Apply@UniTo course page (course 695, intake 'Academic year 2026/27') displays 'Application deadline 8 Sept 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time'. Application fee EUR 60, one-time, non-refundable, payable within the deadline of the call. (b) Applicants holding an ITALIAN university degree (or graduating from an Italian university) do NOT use Apply@UniTo: they submit the SUM 'Preliminary Application for Admission' (Domanda preliminare di ammissione alla magistrale) directly on the www.unito.it / MyUniTO portal, open 3 June - 31 December 2026 for a.y. 2026/2027; the actual enrolment (matriculation) on MyUniTO must then be completed by 14 January 2027, as determined by the Academic Senate. [uncertain - the 3 June - 31 December 2026 window and the 14 January 2027 enrolment deadline were read from search-engine renderings of the live programme page (www.digitalhumanities.unito.it), which is unreachable to direct fetch; the only archived snapshot of that page still shows the previous cycle (1 June - 31 December 2024, enrolment by 17 January 2025)]
application_deadline_non_eu: A.Y. 2026/2027: 29 January 2026. Non-EU citizens residing abroad who need an entry visa can use only the First admission call on Apply@UniTo, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, which is the sole 2026/27 call open to all applicants for postgraduate degree programmes. The Third (1 July - 14 September 2026, restricted-number programmes), Fourth (25 August - 8 September 2026, open-access postgraduate programmes - the call this degree belongs to) and Fifth (25 August - 19 October 2026) calls are all explicitly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy' and are therefore closed to visa applicants; the course page itself warns 'This call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. If you apply without this prerequisite, your application will not be considered.' Places available to this category: 50. In addition, non-EU visa applicants must submit the pre-enrolment (visa) application on the Universitaly platform by 15 July 2026 for a.y. 2026-2027. Application fee EUR 60. [uncertain - the 15 July 2026 Universitaly date is a UNITO-wide deadline published on en.unito.it, which is Cloudflare-blocked to direct fetch and was verified only through search-engine renderings and sibling UNITO programme research; it is not restated on this programme's own pages]
entry_exam_or_test: NO written entrance test (no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT). Admission is by DOSSIER EVALUATION + COMPULSORY ADMISSION INTERVIEW before a Commission of at least three teachers of the Master's Degree course. Apply@UniTo states plainly: 'An admission committee will evaluate applications, based on curriculum and an interview.' The programme's admission-requirements page specifies: 'The admission interview for the degree course is aimed at ascertaining the possession of the basic requirements, necessary to face the master's degree course. In particular, during the interview candidates will be evaluated in relation to their curriculum, with regard to their basic skills with respect to theories and methods in digital humanities, computational techniques and their English language skills.' The interview also serves to verify English proficiency for candidates who do not hold an English certificate. Format and scheduling: interviews 'take place at least once a year, in blended mode and open to the public, upon notice on the degree course website'; in practice several telematic (Cisco Webex) sessions are held per application cycle, each covering the applications received by a stated cut-off date, and candidates receive a personal invitation e-mail from the commission president a few days beforehand. Candidates may request an alternative date, which the Commission will consider if adequately justified. Example schedule from the previous published cycle (a.y. 2024/25, Webex room https://unito.webex.com/meet/andrea.balbo): 11 July 2pm for applications received up to 7 July; 19 September 9am for applications up to 15 September; 5 November 9am for applications up to 31 October; 13 January 2025 9am for applications up to 31 December. [uncertain - the corresponding 2026/2027 interview session dates could not be read: the live programme page is unreachable and the only Wayback snapshot of it carries the 2024/25 schedule]
academic_requirements:
1) DEGREE LEVEL. A Bachelor's degree / three-year university degree (Laurea Triennale) or a qualification obtained abroad recognised as suitable under current legislation; Apply@UniTo: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) gained after at least 3 years of University education.'
2) ELIGIBLE ITALIAN DEGREE CLASSES (curricular requirement route stated on the programme page, D.M. 270 classes): L-1 Cultural Heritage; L-3 Visual Arts, Music, Performing Arts and Fashion Studies; L-5 Philosophy; L-8 Information Engineering; L-10 Literature; L-11 Modern Languages and Cultures; L-12 Linguistic Mediation/Applied Languages; L-15 Tourism Sciences; L-19 Education and Training Sciences; L-20 Communication Sciences; L-31 Computer Science and Technologies; L-42 History; L-43 Technologies for the Conservation and Restoration of Cultural Heritage.
3) CREDIT (ECTS/CFU) REQUIREMENT. At least 54 ECTS across a long list of scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD): INF/01 Informatics; ING-INF/05 Information processing systems; IUS/01 Private Law; IUS/04 Commercial Law; IUS/10 Administrative Law; IUS/19 History of Medieval and Modern Law; L-ANT/03 Roman History; L-ART/01, /02, /03 Medieval, Modern and Contemporary Art History; L-ART/06 Cinema, Photography and Television; L-ART/07 Musicology and History of Music; L-FIL-LET/02 Greek Language and Literature; L-FIL-LET/04 Latin Language and Literature; L-FIL-LET/05 Classical Philology; L-FIL-LET/09 Romance Philology and Linguistics; L-FIL-LET/10 Italian Literature; L-FIL-LET/11 Contemporary Italian Literature; L-FIL-LET/12 Italian Linguistics; L-FIL-LET/13 Philology of Italian Literature; L-FIL-LET/15 Germanic Philology; L-LIN/01 Glottology and Linguistics; L-LIN/03 French Literature; L-LIN/04 French Language and Translation; L-LIN/05 Spanish Literature; L-LIN/06 Hispano-American Languages and Literatures; L-LIN/07 Spanish Language and Translation; L-LIN/10 English Literature; L-LIN/11 Anglo-American Languages and Literatures; L-LIN/12 English Language and Translation; L-LIN/13 German Literature; L-LIN/14 German Language and Translation; L-OR/12 Arabic Language and Literature; L-OR/19 Modern Languages and Literatures of the Indian Subcontinent; L-OR/21 Languages and Literatures of China; L-OR/22 Languages and Literatures of Japan and Korea; M-FIL/02 Logic and Philosophy of Science; M-FIL/04 Aesthetics; M-FIL/05 Philosophy and Theory of Languages; M-FIL/06 History of Philosophy; M-STO/01 Medieval History; M-STO/02 Modern History; M-STO/04 Contemporary History; SPS/07 General Sociology; SPS/08 Sociology of Cultural (and Communication) Processes. Of these 54 ECTS, AT LEAST 18 ECTS must fall in the core sectors INF/01 Informatics, ING-INF/05 Information processing systems, L-FIL-LET/04 Latin Language and Literature, L-FIL-LET/10 Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/11 Contemporary Italian Literature, L-LIN/12 English Language and Translation, M-STO/02 Modern History, M-STO/04 Contemporary History.
4) MINIMUM FINAL GRADE (threshold published on Apply@UniTo for holders of a foreign degree, expressed as a share of the maximum grade): (a) undergraduate degree in Computer Sciences - final grade at least 7.7/10 of the highest possible grade (85/110 for an Italian degree); (b) any other eligible undergraduate degree - final grade at least 8.2/10 of the highest possible grade (90/110 for an Italian degree).
5) PERSONAL PREPARATION. Beyond the curricular requirements, candidates must demonstrate 'adequate personal preparation', assessed by the admission Commission through the dossier and the interview; enrolment is 'subject to a positive evaluation by the Commission responsible for selecting the candidates, which will be composed by at least three teachers from the Master's Degree course'.
6) MISSING CREDITS. Candidates lacking the required SSD credits may, on indication of the degree-course council (CCLM), enrol in single courses (individual teachings) offered by the University and must pass the corresponding assessments BEFORE enrolling in the Master's degree. UNITO students open a ticket through the Student Service Desk (Category: Humanities Pole, Subject: Single courses); non-UNITO students write to servizistudenti.scienzeumanistiche@unito.it with subject 'SINGLE COURSES - MASTER'S DEGREE ADMISSIONS REQUIREMENTS'. Exam results must be communicated by the enrolment deadline of the cycle.
7) PLACES / QUOTA. The programme has non-restricted access, so no general numerus clausus applies; the only published quota is 'This Master's degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.'
8) CONDITIONAL ADMISSION. Applicants who have not yet graduated may apply and be admitted conditionally, but must obtain the bachelor's degree and complete the actual enrolment by the Academic Senate's deadline (14 January 2027 for a.y. 2026/27; 17 January 2025 in the previous published cycle). The programme warns that classes start in mid-September and that conditionally admitted candidates may need to start attending before final confirmation.
language_requirements: ENGLISH - CEFR B2 minimum. The programme's admission-requirements page lists as curricular requirement (c) 'knowledge of the English language at least at B2 level'. Apply@UniTo (course 695) states: 'Applicants must hold an international certification ... certifying at least a CEFR B2 level of English language proficiency. Language certification must be no more than three years old.' Accepted certifications and minimum scores listed by Apply@UniTo: Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE); Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE); Cambridge First Certificate of English (FCE) - minimum score 173 (grade B); PTE Academic - minimum 65; IELTS - minimum 5.5 out of 9, with no component lower than 5.5; TOEFL iBT - minimum 69 out of 120, no component lower than 17; Trinity College ISE II. EXEMPTION / ALTERNATIVE ROUTE: the programme page expressly provides that a certificate is not indispensable - 'If you do not have certificates proving your English skills, these will be verified during the interview', and the interview explicitly assesses 'their English language skills'. ITALIAN - no Italian language requirement: the degree is taught in English, so the UNITO rule requiring an Italian certificate at B2 (CLIQ/CISIA ITA-L2) from non-EU visa applicants applies only to Italian-taught free-access programmes and not to this one. Free 'Learning Italian' support courses are offered to enrolled students (the microsite carries a dedicated 'Learning Italian' page). [uncertain - Apply@UniTo phrases the certificate as mandatory while the programme's own page allows verification at interview instead; the two official sources are not fully aligned, and no explicit waiver is published for applicants whose previous degree was taught in English]
required_documents:
A) PROGRAMME DOSSIER (required by the degree course for the admission Commission, all routes): (1) a copy of the first-level (bachelor's) qualification; (2) the curriculum vitae et studiorum, in Italian or English; (3) any certificate of English language knowledge held (optional - otherwise English is verified at the interview); (4) a cover/motivation letter setting out the candidate's interest in and reasons for enrolling in the Master's Degree in Language Technologies and Digital Humanities and their personal and professional objectives. Apply@UniTo restates this under 'Other requirements': 'A motivation letter must be added to your application.'
B) DOMESTIC ROUTE (Italian degree holders, SUM preliminary application on MyUniTO): the online form must be filled in with the exams taken, specifying SSD, CFU and grade, and the following must be attached: the self-certification of passed exams and the documents proving that the entry requirements are met (i.e. the dossier in A). Non-UNITO graduates must first register on the www.unito.it portal to obtain credentials; UNITO graduates use their existing UNITO credentials.
C) APPLY@UNITO ROUTE (holders of a foreign qualification), in addition to A: valid identity document / passport (passport for non-EU citizens; residence permit valid for university enrolment for non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy); the first-cycle degree certificate obtained after at least 3 years of university education (or evidence that it will be obtained in time); the official academic transcript of records showing exams, SSD/subject areas, credits and grades - needed to verify the 54 ECTS / 18 ECTS core-sector and final-grade thresholds; the motivation letter in English or Italian; English language certification where held; optionally the degree programme syllabus (course descriptions) issued by the foreign institution with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish; documents required for the applicant's specific foreign education system; payment of the EUR 60 non-refundable application fee within the call deadline (the same amount whether one or two programmes are chosen). LANGUAGE OF DOCUMENTS: 'The entry qualification documents are accepted in the following languages: English / French / Italian / Spanish. If the document is issued in a different language from those listed above, you will have to upload both the original document and its certified translation.' AFTER SUBMISSION: UNITO may request further documents - Declaration of Value, Statement of Verification, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability - and the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment stage. Non-EU visa applicants must in addition complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment application (one programme only) with the competent Italian embassy/consulate.

uncertainty_notes:
1) ACCESS PROBLEM. The programme microsite www.digitalhumanities.unito.it, www.unito.it and en.unito.it could not be fetched directly during this research: the unito.it origin refused/timed out every direct connection, and the r.jina.ai reader returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge. Only apply.unito.it (externally hosted on DreamApply) and the Wayback Machine responded. The Cineca national catalogue (unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it) returned an HTTP 405 'Human Verification' page. Content from the microsite was therefore reconstructed from (a) Wayback snapshots - admission_requirements.html of 17 June 2025 (page content last updated 28/05/2024, i.e. the a.y. 2024/25 cycle), key_information.html of 16 April 2026 (last updated 21/07/2025, covering a.y. 2023/24-2025/26), how_to_apply.html of 17 June 2025 - and (b) verbatim search-engine renderings of the live pages. A CDX index scan found only ONE archived snapshot of the admission-requirements page, so the current 2026/27 wording could not be read in full context.
2) TEACHING LANGUAGE is unambiguous: fully English-taught, single-university (Department of Humanities, University of Turin), not interuniversity, not a pathway/curriculum inside an Italian-named degree. However, TEACHING MODE is officially 'Blended' - prospective students should be aware that delivery mixes in-person and online components, and the admission interview is held remotely (Cisco Webex).
3) 2026/27 DOMESTIC DATES. The preliminary-application window 3 June - 31 December 2026 and the enrolment deadline 14 January 2027 come from search-engine renderings of the live admission-requirements page and could not be confirmed against a directly fetched or archived page; the only archived version still shows the previous cycle (1 June - 31 December 2024, enrolment by 17 January 2025). These dates should be re-verified once unito.it is reachable.
4) INTERVIEW DATES for a.y. 2026/2027 are unknown. The dates listed in this record (11 July / 19 September / 5 November / 13 January) belong to the a.y. 2024/25 cycle and are given only as an indication of the typical rhythm (roughly four telematic sessions per cycle, each with an application cut-off a few days earlier). The programme itself states the published dates are indicative and that candidates receive a personal invitation e-mail from the commission president shortly before their interview.
5) TWO DIFFERENT FORMULATIONS OF THE ACADEMIC REQUIREMENT. The programme page expresses the curricular requirement as a list of eligible Italian degree classes (L-1 ... L-43) plus 54 ECTS/18 ECTS in named SSDs, with no minimum grade. Apply@UniTo, addressing holders of foreign degrees, instead adds explicit minimum final-grade thresholds (7.7/10 for Computer Science degrees, 8.2/10 otherwise) and reproduces the SSD credit lists. The two sources are complementary rather than contradictory, but the grade thresholds appear ONLY on Apply@UniTo, and no official page explains how the Italian degree-class list is mapped onto foreign qualifications - the admission Commission decides case by case.
6) TRANSCRIPTION DEFECT ON APPLY@UNITO. In the Apply@UniTo 'Entry qualification' text, the 18-ECTS core-sector list is garbled: it reads 'ING-INF/05 - Latin Language and Literature', evidently merging the code ING-INF/05 with the label of L-FIL-LET/04. The programme page's version of the same list (INF/01, ING-INF/05, L-FIL-LET/04, L-FIL-LET/10, L-FIL-LET/11, L-LIN/12, M-STO/02, M-STO/04) is the correct one and has been used here.
7) ENGLISH CERTIFICATE - CONFLICTING STRICTNESS. Apply@UniTo presents the B2 certificate as mandatory ('Applicants must hold an international certification'), while the programme's own admission page treats it as optional evidence and provides that English is otherwise verified at the interview. Applicants without a certificate should confirm with the programme before applying through Apply@UniTo, where the online form may block submission without an uploaded certificate.
8) NON-EU QUOTA AND CALL. The 50-place non-EU-abroad quota is confirmed on the live Apply@UniTo page for a.y. 2026/27. Because this is an open-access postgraduate programme, non-EU applicants residing abroad had only the First admission call (closed 29 January 2026); at the time of research (1 September 2026) no call open to that category remained for a.y. 2026/2027.
9) UNIVERSITALY. The 15 July 2026 visa pre-enrolment deadline is a UNITO-wide/national deadline taken from en.unito.it via search-engine rendering (en.unito.it stays Cloudflare-blocked); it is not restated on this programme's own pages.
10) FEES. The EUR 2,800/year figure quoted by Apply@UniTo is the a.y. 2025-26 maximum of an income-based (ISEE) range starting at EUR 156; the a.y. 2026-27 bands are published separately on the UNITO fee pages. Unlike some UNITO English-taught degrees (e.g. Business & Management), no additional programme-specific contribution is advertised for this degree. Part-time enrolment changes the fee.
